Craft · Vision

The glass, the table, the details.

NASHA should look like one company wherever you look: the plate, the glass, the apron, the sign. Structure over souvenir.

Everything here is a vision drawing. Glass makers, fabric, tableware and signage have not been chosen, and none of it is tested or approved.

How to read this site
Vision
What NASHA could become. Most of this site.
Prototype
What the founder has physically made. Nothing yet.
Validated
What has passed a test we defined in advance. Nothing yet.

The vision is a design to aim at. The business view says what is real, what is assumed and what still needs proof.

Three glasses tell the story better than five.

A tall Signature Hefe glass, a versatile Lager and Pils glass, an aromatic option for amber and Witbier, plus a small flight tulip. This is a vision choice; the earlier five-glass concept remains in the blueprint. Whether the shapes can be made, stacked and washed is not verified.

Signature Hefe glassTall, with a raised ring. Hefeweizen.
Lager and Pils glassA refined cone. Lager and Pilsner.
Aromatic glassA short tulip. Amber and Witbier.

Zero-proof, equal in care

Same clear glass, natural colour, one simple garnish. Not children's soda, not a mocktail cliché, not a garnish tower. Flavour plans only; none is tested.

Ritual

A small moment of care.

A clean glass on a coaster of ceramic or wood. For the Hefeweizen, a two-step pour at the table, only if testing shows it is worth the time. Brass and woven fibre where they have a job to do. No smoke, no dry ice, no flames, no tricks.

Say it plainly

  • Bright bubbles reset your mouth after each bite. Cleansing
  • Cool and crisp against hot and rich. Contrast
  • The beer smells like something already on the plate. Shared aroma
  • A little sourness keeps rich food light. Acid
  • It calms the chile without wiping it out. Heat relief
  • Soft and creamy against crisp and charred. Texture

The rest of the world

Pattern, people, signage, packaging, sound.

The small things that make it one company. Each opens when you want it.

Pattern: perforation, weave, tile

Three simple structures: a screen pierced with circles, strips woven over and under, a tile grid with a broken line. Designers can find parallels for each in many cultures; none is borrowed from a specific one. It appears sparingly (the screen, a menu, a coaster) and cultural reviewers from both traditions must check it before it is used outside a drawing.

Uniforms that work, not costumes

Charcoal canvas aprons over bone shirts for the floor and bar. Dark work shirts and boots for the brewers. Dark jackets for the kitchen. Nothing themed, nothing printed across the chest.

Signage: material first, name second

A plain blackened-steel panel on a concrete plinth, a slim blade sign under the arcade, a small plaque on the door. The lettering is a placeholder. The name is not legally cleared and there is no logo, so the building is designed to work if the name changes.

Takeout, coaster, bag, napkin

Concept drawings with no real labels. No alcohol label is shown or implied as compliant.

Sound: a room you can talk in

Quiet and warm by day, building gently into the evening. No stock India-plus-Mexico playlist. A small acoustic set might fit one corner. Licensing and permits are unresolved.

NASHA is a future Indo-Mex brewery and kitchen in Austin, Texas, in development. Nothing is open or for sale, and no site has been chosen. Pictures are concept visualizations or drawings, not photographs of NASHA.

Name, images and allergens

The name was chosen by the founder; legal clearance is pending and nothing here claims trademark ownership. The word NASHA in the header and in some pictures is a temporary typographic placeholder, not a logo. Nasha means intoxication or addiction in Hindi and Urdu: we chose it for the feeling of being drawn in by food, craft and company, we will never present excess as something to admire, and cultural advisors will review the name and our language before launch.

Photographic-style pictures are concept visualizations made with AI tools and edited; drawings are illustrations. None is a photograph of NASHA, its food or its beer (about these images). Dishes are designs for testing, not served food; heat and vegetarian labels are design intent, not a certified allergen or dietary statement. Ask before you eat if you have an allergy. If you drink, drink responsibly; alcohol is for adults of legal drinking age.
